technical_and_design_decisions: Implement each source and sink as a separately configurable Spring Integration-style module following the existing module lifecycle, message, metadata, and configuration conventions.
Implement the WebSocket source using Spring WebSocket support with configurable endpoint, session handling, message conversion, and browser-origin controls.

Implement the AWS source with adapters for S3 ingestion and SES event/message ingestion, using the AWS SDK and configurable credentials, region, polling or notification behavior, and object/message conversion.
Implement AWS S3 output as a sink with configurable bucket, key strategy, region, credentials, content serialization, and upload error handling.
Implement the Cassandra sink using the DataStax Java driver with configurable contact points, keyspace, table, consistency, batching, prepared statements, and schema mapping.
Implement the HAWQ sink behind a pluggable writer abstraction that serializes records to Avro or Parquet and writes them through the configured PXF-compatible integration path.
Implement the Solr sink using SolrJ with configurable collection, endpoint, document mapping, commit behavior, batching, and retry handling.

Implement error-channel support as a framework-level interception and routing mechanism covering source, processor, sink, and custom-module failures; preserve the root cause and expose configurable exception matching and error-channel destinations.
Treat partition-state preservation as an existing production capability and add regression and dynamic module add/delete tests rather than modifying the partitioning implementation.
Use automated unit tests, contract tests, and external-service integration tests with containers or local test doubles where practical; isolate tests requiring real AWS, HAWQ, or Solr services.
assumptions: An existing Java 17+ Spring-based project, build system, module framework, configuration mechanism, and CI pipeline are available and follow recognizable conventions.
The estimate covers implementation, tests, documentation, and integration of the requested increment, but not redesign of the existing framework or migration of unrelated modules.
The AWS source must support both S3 ingestion and SES ingestion, with SES consumed through its standard notification or message-delivery integration rather than implementing an SMTP server.
AWS authentication uses standard SDK credential-provider-chain support; production IAM policy design, account provisioning, and infrastructure deployment are excluded.
The Cassandra, Solr, and HAWQ services and test credentials are available for integration testing, or representative containers and stubs can be used when a service cannot run locally.
HAWQ access is available through an agreed PXF-compatible endpoint or client contract. Implementing or modifying HAWQ, PXF, Avro, or Parquet internals is excluded.
Existing serialization, schema mapping, retry, back-pressure, and observability facilities are reused where available.
Backward compatibility is required for existing modules and configurations, but no support for unspecified legacy versions is included.

The error-channel feature supports configurable exception matching, the requested GlobalException, DefaultException, and ModuleSpecificException hierarchy, root-cause preservation, and continuation where the existing runtime permits recovery; business-specific recovery policies are excluded.
One developer performs the work, and the effort values represent active work-hours rather than elapsed calendar time or waiting time for external environments.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing module architecture and conventions, refine configuration and message contracts for all requested modules, identify compatibility constraints, and produce the implementation design and task breakdown.
Add or update module registrations, build dependencies, configuration schemas, shared serialization and credential handling, lifecycle wiring, and common test fixtures required by the new modules.
Implement the WebSocket endpoint and session/message adapters, browser event conversion, configuration, lifecycle behavior, validation, error propagation, unit tests, and module-level documentation.

Implement S3 ingestion and SES ingestion adapters, AWS SDK configuration and credential handling, polling or notification processing, payload conversion, retries, validation, unit tests, and service-level integration tests.

Implement Cassandra connection and session management, prepared and batched writes, configurable table and consistency behavior, record-to-column mapping, error handling, unit tests, and Cassandra integration tests.

Implement S3 object creation and upload, key and content serialization strategies, configurable AWS settings, batching or multipart behavior as appropriate, retry and failure handling, unit tests, and integration tests.

Implement Avro and Parquet serialization, PXF-compatible delivery, configurable target and schema settings, buffering and flush behavior, failure handling, test doubles, format tests, and HAWQ/PXF integration tests.
Implement SolrJ connectivity, document mapping, collection and commit configuration, batching and retry behavior, error handling, unit tests, and Solr integration tests.

Implement framework-level failure interception for source, processor, sink, and custom modules; preserve complete cause chains; add configurable channel routing and exception matching; implement the requested exception hierarchy; support continuation semantics; and add focused unit and integration tests.

Create regression tests covering preservation of partition strategy state and dynamic adaptation when modules are added or deleted, including representative source, processor, and sink configurations.

Test module composition, configuration loading, message contracts, error routing across complete pipelines, retry and restart behavior, compatibility with existing modules, and representative end-to-end scenarios.
Document configuration properties, credentials, endpoint setup, payload and schema mappings, operational limitations, error-channel usage, and example pipelines for each requested capability.

Run the complete build and test suite, perform static analysis and dependency checks, resolve integration defects, review configuration and API compatibility, and prepare the release or merge artifacts.
